reference_formalization: ∀ (a b c d e f : Point) (AB BC AC DE EF DF : Line), formTriangle a b c AB BC AC ∧ formTriangle d e f DE EF DF ∧ (|(a─b)| = |(d─e)|) ∧ (|(a─c)| = |(d─f)|) ∧ (|(b─c)| > |(e─f)|) → (∠ b:a:c > ∠ e:d:f)
nl_statement: If two triangles have two sides equal to two sides, respectively, but (one) has a base greater than the base (of the other), then (the former triangle) will also have the angle encompassed by the equal straight-lines greater than the (corresponding) angle (in the latter).Let $ABC$ and $DEF$ be  two triangles having the two sides $AB$ and $AC$ equal to the two sides $DE$ and $DF$, respectively. (That is), $AB$ (equal) to $DE$, and $AC$ to $DF$. And let the base $BC$ be greater than the base $EF$. I say that angle $BAC$ is also greater than $EDF$. <prf>  Thus, $BAC$ is greater than $EDF$.Thus, if two triangles have two sides equal to two sides, respectively, but (one) has a base greater than the base (of the other), then (the former triangle) will also have the angle encompassed by the equal straight-lines greater than the (corresponding) angle (in the latter).
